info.name: Google Flow (labs.google) — Reverse-Engineered API
info.description:
Endpoints Google Flow (labs.google/flow, formerly VideoFX/ImageFX) uses internally, reverse-engineered from browser HAR captures for OrinoFlow's automation layer (see src-tauri/src/commands/imagegen.rs).

This is a **private, undocumented Google API** — not a public product. It requires:

1. A real, logged-in `labs.google` session (cookies: `__Secure-1PSID`/session cookies + the `access_token` returned by `GET /fx/api/auth/session`).
2. For any *generation* call (`batchGenerateImages`, `upsampleImage`, all `video:batchAsyncGenerate*`, `batchAsyncGenerateVideoUpsampleVideo`), a **reCAPTCHA Enterprise token** minted client-side via `grecaptcha.enterprise.execute(SITEKEY, {action:...})` in an actual browser context with site key `6LdsFiUsAAAAAIjVDZcuLhaHiDn5nnHVXVRQGeMV`. Postman cannot generate this token — you must copy one out of DevTools/a HAR capture (it's short-lived, ~2 min) before firing these requests, or these calls will fail even with a valid session.

Host split:
- `labs.google` — session/auth, tRPC project & entity endpoints, video upload, media URL resolution. Auth = session **cookies**.
- `aisandbox-pa.googleapis.com` — the actual generation/media-mutation API. Auth = **Bearer {{accessToken}}** (from `/fx/api/auth/session`).

Set `{{cookie}}` to your full `labs.google` cookie string and `{{accessToken}}` to `access_token` from the session call before running anything beyond folder 1.

variable.description: Full Cookie header value copied from a logged-in labs.google browser session.
Fresh grecaptcha.enterprise token, action must match the endpoint (IMAGE_GENERATION or VIDEO_GENERATION). Short-lived.

request.description: Returns { access_token, ... } for the logged-in labs.google session. Copy `access_token` into the `accessToken` collection variable — every aisandbox-pa.googleapis.com call needs it as a Bearer token.
tRPC mutation. Response: result.data.json.result.projectId — save into `projectId`.

tRPC query (GET, params via `input`). Response shape confirmed via HAR: result.data.json.result.projects[] = { projectId, projectInfo:{ projectTitle, thumbnailMediaKey }, creationTime }.

Set the `searchProjectsInput` variable to the URL-encoded JSON shown above (pageSize max observed = 20).
Full project snapshot: result.data.json.projectContents = { workflows[], media[], entities[] }. Used to list characters/images/videos and to recover an in-flight generation after a client crash.

body.raw:
{
  "clientContext": { "projectId": "{{projectId}}", "tool": "PINHOLE" },
  "imageBytes": "<base64 image bytes, no data: prefix>",
  "isUserUploaded": true,
  "isHidden": false,
  "mimeType": "image/png",
  "fileName": "ref.png"
}

request.description: No reCAPTCHA needed. `isHidden:false` makes it show up in the project's media tab (used for plain user uploads); reference/base images used only as generation input are typically also isHidden:false in this app. Response: media.name → mediaId.

reCAPTCHA action must be `IMAGE_GENERATION`. `imageAspectRatio` one of: IMAGE_ASPECT_RATIO_LANDSCAPE | _PORTRAIT | _SQUARE | _LANDSCAPE_FOUR_THREE | _PORTRAIT_THREE_FOUR.

`imageInputs[]` entries: `{ imageInputType: 'IMAGE_INPUT_TYPE_REFERENCE', name: <mediaId> }` for reference/@-mentioned character images, or `{ imageInputType: 'IMAGE_INPUT_TYPE_BASE_IMAGE', name: <mediaId> }` when editing an existing image in place.

This same endpoint is also used to generate a character's slot image — add `mediaGenerationContext.entityContext = { entityId, characterSlot: { imageReferenceIndex } }` (new slot) or set `clientContext.workflowId` + a BASE_IMAGE input (editing an existing slot) instead of a plain new-media call.

Response: media[0].image.generatedImage.fifeUrl (signed download URL) + media[0].name (mediaId). When entity/workflow context is used, also read workflows[0].name for the new workflowId.

`targetResolution`: UPSAMPLE_IMAGE_RESOLUTION_2K | UPSAMPLE_IMAGE_RESOLUTION_4K. Synchronous — response returns immediately with `media.name` (new mediaId) and `encodedImage` (base64 bytes), no polling needed (unlike video upscale).

Step 1/3 of adding a character: creates an empty 'Untitled Character' entity. Response: result.data.json.entityId. Step 2 is 'Generate images' above with mediaGenerationContext.entityContext. Step 3 is 'Patch entity' below to save displayName + imageReferences.
`updateMask` lists only the fields you want Google to apply — send just `entityInfo.displayName` for a pure rename without touching imageReferences.

Run after editing an existing character-slot image in place (workflowId unchanged, only the representative media changes). Also used to attach an uploaded local video's media as the primary media of its workflow.
Generic asset-deletion endpoint; this app only feeds it entityIds (character deletion), but presumably also accepts other asset id fields for media/workflow deletion.

reCAPTCHA action `VIDEO_GENERATION`. `videoModelKey` encodes core+mode+duration+priority — no separate durationSeconds field. Examples confirmed via HAR:
- veo_3_1_t2v_lite_low_priority (text, 8s default)
- veo_3_1_t2v_lite_4s_low_priority (4s)
See `resolve_video_model_key` in imagegen.rs for the full core×mode×duration matrix (veo_3_1_quality/fast/lite, abra Omni Flash, i2v/r2v/t2v/edit infixes, `_fl` suffix for first+last-frame).

Async — response returns workflows[0] with metadata.primaryMediaId (pending mediaId) and name (workflowId); poll status below until it resolves.
`startImage.mediaId` must already exist in the project (upload via 'Upload image' first). `cropCoordinates` full-frame = {top:0,left:0,bottom:1,right:1}.

`videoModelKey` uses the `_fl` suffix ("first+last") — e.g. veo_3_1_i2v_s_lite_6s_fl / _quality_6s_fl. Google has no 'end frame only' endpoint — an end image without a start image is simply dropped by the app.

Same endpoint serves two mutually-exclusive input styles — send EITHER `referenceImages[]` (uploaded reference photos) OR `referenceEntities` (array of character entity refs for @-mentions), not both.

`videoModelKey` is forced to `abra_edit`. `endFrameIndex` = duration_in_seconds * 24fps (8s → 192). NOTE (confirmed via HAR): this is the one video-submit body that does NOT include `useV2ModelConfig`. Optional `referenceImages[]` (IMAGE_USAGE_TYPE_ASSET) can be added alongside videoInput.

1080p: resolution VIDEO_RESOLUTION_1080P + videoModelKey veo_3_1_upsampler_1080p → operation name `{mediaId}_upsampled`.
4K: resolution VIDEO_RESOLUTION_4K + videoModelKey veo_3_1_upsampler_4k → operation name `{mediaId}_4k_upsampled` (different suffix).

Response: operations[0].operation.name is the new (pending) media id to poll on.

Poll target for every async video/upscale/upload submission — batch multiple `media[]` entries in one call to check several jobs at once. Read `media[].mediaMetadata.mediaStatus.mediaGenerationStatus`: MEDIA_GENERATION_STATUS_PENDING (keep polling) → _ACTIVE → _SUCCESSFUL | _FAILED. Respect a `Retry-After` response header / 429 by backing off (this app polls every ~5-10s, capped backoff up to 5 min).
Empty body but Content-Length: 0 must be explicit (server 411s without it on some HTTP clients — not usually an issue from Postman/browsers but was for Rust's reqwest). Response: { sessionUrl }.
Body = raw video bytes (attach the file in Postman's Body > binary tab). Response: { status: 'final', mediaServerId, workflowServerId, videoWidth, videoHeight }.
`mediaId` = mediaServerId from step 2. `endOffset` = actual clip duration in seconds, e.g. '8s'.
Reuses the same status endpoint as generation — poll until mediaGenerationStatus leaves MEDIA_GENERATION_STATUS_PENDING.
Final step — same call as folder 4's 'Patch workflow primaryMediaId'. `workflowId` here = workflowServerId from step 2.

query.description: Optional — omit for full/raw media, set to request a thumbnail variant instead.

request.description: Do NOT let Postman auto-follow the 3xx here if you want to inspect the signed CDN URL — this call requires labs.google session cookies, but the redirect target (flow-content.google, a signed URL) does not and should be fetched separately/without cookies. In Postman: disable 'Automatically follow redirects' in Settings, or just inspect the Location response header, then GET that URL in a fresh request.
